item.title: SCP Reference Help
item.content:encoded:
I've seen a number of SCPs myself, but not enough. So at the moment there are 2 ideas that might have some potential.

1) An object that can observe past histories

2) A D-class that does not die

.

With the first, I originally concepted this object being a magnifying glass, however I did note after conception that there's a magnifying glass entry on some knock-off SCP website that refers to themselves as scp classic? Store, cache, preserve? Even if it isn't canon I think my concept can be mixed up a bit more than taking that specific form.

The key element is that this object would be able to reference an edit log for anything that is seen through it. You know, how on some of these posts you can see an edit history? That's the idea, but it could be all contents ever written on a whiteboard. Or in a notebook. But even deeper, say in a long held manuscript; like the Quran, or the Bible. Maybe even ████████ material? Naturally the key to this concept would be in the story surrounding it, but I want to know if this idea exists in the scp lore in anyway. I'm sure people have used time travel in their creation, but this specific trait just might be limiting enough to push a tale.

I do comprehend, being able to see redacted material is a dangerous idea, being that author makes that information unavailable to guide the mystery of it. But if used correctly, it has good potential to revive an old topic. Obviously requires a test of scrutiny.

.

The second concept is a lesser one in which I simply considered: What if there was a D-class that always survived their testing? If we apply this nature to a soldier or a doctor? Sure, there is some possibility, but D-class always gets the worst of it. So again, I want to know if there's any D-class that are SCPs.

This idea has less wiggle room being, at the moment, it's just an entity with writers shield. But there might be some fun to be had with this concept. P.S. I am not thinking of a character trait like Marvel's Darwin, where his body just adapts to any situation. Not my intent what-so-ever. Nor do I wish to pursue some "he's just lucky" trait akin to Domino. What would the D-class be I dunno, but I don't want to start concepting if there's already another similar D-class on the list.

.

If you can help I'd dearly appreciate it.


Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Questions Desk
Forum thread: SCP Reference Help

I'm having some issues with this skip.

+ Structural Issues

Problem 1: I find the crossed-out information an annoyance to read. Typically, I would be fine with it, but there are at least five instances of it here. Either the crossed-out information is not important (In which case, why is it included?), or, the crossed-out information is of special importance (In which case, why is there a hurdle to read it?).

Possible Solution A: I suggest erring on the side of simply not including any of the information that you cross out.

Problem 2: I'm confused about the -1 instances. Is the assumption that -1 refers to elders who drilled a hole into their cranium? If that is the case, why is that not explicitly stated? I had to reread the paragraph that introduces -1 several times, but still came away from it doubtful that I'd had the right idea.

Possible Solution B: It would aid the reader if (1) the process of transformation were stated explicitly (instead of leading the reader to believe an entirely new entity was created — which isn't the case), and (2) the biological makeup of -1 instances were mentioned. If -1 instances are elders with an anomaly which allows computer interface via biomechanical attachment in the cranium — say so.

Problem 3: There are several instances of imprecise wording, like "various". I'm never sure as to the criteria being used when "various" is referred to. For instance:

A computing company that creates various anomalous programs and products.

What kind of anomalous programs do Slum's create?

SCP-5896 is functionally identical to the Windows 95 operating system with various minor cosmetic changes.

What kind of cosmetic changes?

Occasionally, various computer components will grow within SCP-5896-1 instances; […]

What kind of computer component grows beneath the skin?

These vagueries make it difficult to picture what's being described because they forcibly deprive a reader of imagery. This is not what you want in an SCP unless there is a prescribed reason for it (like a meta infohazardous anomaly associated with the document).

Possible Solution C: Consider what disadvantage a researcher in-universe might have if they were presented this same (low) level of information on something that's Keter. If your intent is not to elaborate, then you can simply omit the "various". And I understand that it later specifies one of the computer growths is a -2 instance, but the reader is still led to believe it can cause something else. Instead of promoting imagination, this is enabling confusion, when you can instead word things slightly different and achieve much better effect.

- Close
+ Narrative Issues

Here are the places where I think the narrative is lacking:

  1. How did the Foundation recognize this was anomalous before they tested it? I don't see why they might have had the copies in their possession in the first place. But because there is no Discovery, this question is left unaddressed. This isn't necessarily a question I feel like I'm working toward as a reader — it instead feels like a lack of development.
  2. Did they really terminate the employment of Dr. Reynolds, yet neither keep track of him after the fact nor amnesticize him?

These two issues are minor, but they paint a bit of a picture of what I might consider Foundation negligence. Now, you can absolutely tell that kind of story — one of a corrupt organization; of an organization with misplaced values; or systemic issues. Narratives about corporate/bureaucratic shortcomings are certainly in no shortage, and they paint a more realistic setting (which I personally favour). But when Foundation negligence is introduced on its own without any real justification, it feels out of character.

- Close

Overall: I can see you were aiming for a short and direct skip. For the most part, I think you succeed! But I think the instances of less-than-adequately executed 'negative space' (where the reader is asked to piece things together on their own instead of being explicitly told things) are less of a feature and more of a bug. Especially considering the gap this creates in the reader's understanding of what's going on, paired with imprecise language. I think this skip has a truly visceral body horror idea about it and would have wanted it to shine more.

item.title: Re: The thrilling world of Foundation bureaucracy
item.content:encoded:
Thank you for the crit :)

The issue of mundanity is definitely a great point. Originally I was going for a less intensive, purposefully weak object that took a backseat to what an internal investigation within the foundation might look like, and how an organization with zero transparency might carry out, or fail to do that. This has turned out to be a bit of a miss. Either scaling down the story (focusing on the little white lies of bureaucracy with a site manager trying to cover for themselves rather than the top brass) or scaling up the object seems like the way to go.

My plan was, since the foundation never finds out when the object ended up on site, to have the origins remain a mystery, but I see how that could definitely be unsatisfying despite that being the intention.

As for the image, I'm not really sure what I can do to aid that other than attempting to mess around with it in photoshop or something that I've never used before, I do see where you are coming from with that though.

Thanks again so much for the crit and extra pair of eyes on this, you've been a massive help!

item.title: Re: First time SCP: revealing the truth?
item.content:encoded:
There's nothing really to this currently. Weird laptop. Why is it even an anomaly? This could just be a hacker who has an algorithm that will continually release classified documents, etc.

More importantly, try to answer the following questions and then edit your post accordingly.

+ show block
– hide block

You get 400 words in the last four sections of the post to expand upon your idea, so I think that you should attempt to explore this further. This does not mean providing a link to the draft. This is about convincing people that you have a good idea and the ability to sell that good idea.

What are the stakes of this anomaly? - in it's current form, why couldn't the foundation just throw it in a box and forget about it?

What will you do to get the reader to feel invested in these events? Is there someone we can relate to?

What is the narrative journey of the article? Where do we start and then where do we end?

What is the thematic core to your article? What are you trying to say?

item.title: [Seeking Greenlights] The Ambassador's Strolling Players
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Horror

Elevator Pitch: The Foundation's researchers are invited to take in a terrible show and rewarded with intelligence at the cost of nightmares.

Central Narrative:

+ show block
– hide block

A Foundation researcher discovers a letter on their desk, inviting them to join a fellow scholar in taking in a show. The letter comes with a ticket to see "The Ambassador's Strolling Players" and instructions to burn it on a certain time and date.

Under heavy monitoring, the researcher complies and is transported to what appears to be a renaissance era opera house. Once arrived he is greeted by a strange crow man who tells him to stay silent through the performance and meet him back by concessions during the intermission.

The crow man then sits the researcher down in a massive theater filled with other strange creatures. On stage a disturbing show is performed showing a group of masked individuals convincing a strange creature they have its best interests at heart before betraying it in the end.

An intermission is called and the crow man joins the researcher by the concession stand. He says he needs to say as little as possible, and nothing even resembling a name can be used here. He hands the doctor a packet filled with enhanced containment procedures for some of the Foundation's most nasty SCPs.

They watch the conclusion of the play, seeing the "heroes" in masks bringing forth all of the riches they stole from the strange creature before "The Ambassador" who accepts them with a nod, which the masked actors receive with almost orgasmic delight.

Then the crow creature offers the researcher "a lift back" and teleports the researcher back to the test site before leaving.

The containment strategies the crow creature provided prove to be extremely effective in preventing breaches.

Other researchers in the Foundation begin receiving similar messages, inviting them to see other grotesque plays in exchange for valuable intelligence.

This goes on for some time until at one point, a researcher arrives at the opera house to see the actor who played "The Ambassador" in the crow's place. It gives the researcher a box that turns out to contain the crow's head and the researcher arrives back at home.

No further tickets are received.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: "Most likely SCP-XXXX is neutralized, but if you receive a ticket, you are to await an O5 vote before taking further action. Someone out there took a big risk to help us and it cost him everything. We cannot allow it to cost us everything too."

Additional Notes: I look forward to your comments!

item.title: Re: SCP concept Investigator Poz
item.content:encoded:
Responding to IRC Chat request.

This tells me effectively nothing of what your article is going to detail. It's mysterious blank after mysterious blank, and too many blank spots inches closer and closer to nothing being said. Furthermore, an investigator that stumbles onto anomalies (obviously barring the amnestic thing) does not necessarily mean they are anomalous themselves, which is what the SCP format is about: documenting objects and entities that otherwise defy our understanding of modern science.

Altogether, there is no information here that indicates that this is ready to be made into an article. It's undercooked. I would suggest taking a moment to consider the following:

  • What kind of story do you want to tell?
  • What are the key points in that story?
  • How do you plan to showcase that in the SCP format?
  • What do you find entertaining about the article?

item.title: Ultimate Digital Assistant
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: No

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Unsure. It doesn't fit into anything else

Page Layout (Optional): Classic

Elevator Pitch: SCP-XXXX is an entity on a phone that knows things, even in the future, to excruciating detail. It also calls itself "Watson"

Central Narrative: SCP-XXXX is an entity that took the place of Siri on an iPhone that sounds like a British Male. The tip of the iceberg is that it knows anything about anything non-anomalous. For example, ask it about what someone else ate for lunch on a certain day, and SCP-XXXX will tell what that person ate, down to the brand of the ingredients and where they came from. It doesn't know anything about anomalous objects though. It will say "I don't have any information on that."

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The dark side of SCP-XXXX is that its voice will progressively become raspier and raspier and filled with coughs over time. Once exactly three months pass, one person with a voice matching a Man with a British Accent within a range of 70 meters disappears and SCP-XXXX's voice will become clear again. If no one who fits the bill is within range, a random person will vanish and SCP-XXXX will change to that person's voice. SCP-XXXX says that this happens because it needs to sustain itself and "Don't worry about the disappearances".

Additional Notes: I have a feeling this has been done before or something similar has popped up, I'll need to know. I'll elaborate more on its personality if need be or how testing logs would play out or progress.

item.title: SCP concept Investigator Poz
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Hook: A Private Investigator has been seen at multiple (31) instances near newly discovered SCPs. Seems to be unaffected by many SCPs and Amnestics.

Central Narrative: Investigator Poz has been very elusive to the foundation and could be used as an asset. He, also, seems to know of SCPs and how to find them. Recently he has been seen to be unaffected by SCP-XXXX (Death-bringer #324) an SCP that predicts deaths. He was also unaffected by SCP-XXXX (Nightshift Hellscape) a place that affects people beyond repair mentally or otherwise. Investigator Poz has not been located as of yet.

Page Layout: Containment procedures and SCP information first. Then the instances of where he has been sighted.

Elevator Pitch: The Private Investigator known as Investigator Howard Poz has been spotted at multiple sites of SCPs (31 known instances). He is drawn to SCPs for some anomalous reason not yet discovered. The reason the foundation knows this is an anomalous property is because he has found 3 in Russia, 2 in China, 4 in Canada, 12 across the USA, 3 in Brazil etc. Finding one or two is natural, but finding 31 before the foundation is unnatural. He seems to be unaffected by amnestics up to Class C if not more. All the SCPs he has been seen at are newly discovered. The foundation does not know if he is creating the SCPs or just discovering them. If the latter is true he could make a good asset for the foundation. However if the former is true, we need to take immediate action to secure the Investigator.

Level 3 Clearance required

The SCP known as Investigator Poz has been catalogued with 3 anomalous properties.
1. Immunity to Amnestics
2. Immunity to most SCP affects
3. The ability to create beings or objects with anomalous properties

Level 4 Clearance required

Based on interviews from the populace who have met the Investigator, he has stated that he is "cataloging" and "trying to prevent the utter destruction of the world."

Additional Notes: SCPs he has been spotted at will be recorded

item.title: Re: *Seeking Greenlight* Mu-13-C "Cats Eye"
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

then it was going to have an initial experiment log that I was going to use the experiment log format style I found.

I am not convinced a test log would work with cats seeing specters. Why not just a summary of findings in the Description? Honestly, although the origin of the site has deep ties to test logs… I personally rarely find them interesting… And think a simple paragraph explaining what research has revealed to flow better.

in my draft I have it that the cat with experience a piloerection in its tail and begin to growl while following the entity with its eyes and this would alert the MTF to its presents.

I guess you might relate them to how Ghost hunter shows misuse EMF readers too find ghosts but these would actually work.

Well, this doesn't really answer my question. Because an EMF reader is a machine that you can hold. A cat is not. So how does an MTF utilize a cat in the field? Let them loose in the area and follow them around? Keep them in cages? Good luck getting a cat to go where you want them to is my point.

So while I am fairly sure of the plot of your article: Researcher discovers cats can see ghosts -> confirms with testing -> proposes they be used with MTFs -> and we follow their use in the field; That plot really doesn't tell me much about the narrative. Is there a thematic arc to this? Where does the reader start, and what is the journey they go on?

Moreover, I would recommend against the note at the end trope for your first article. Its overused, Lots of us are guilty of it… but I feel like you're going to get some heat for trying it in the end of the first article you use. Also, it just isn't usually satisfying without a big reveal. This, as proposed, is more of the "next logical step." Probably more interesting to give us a log of the cats being used in the field, make that interesting and just end with "Further use of SCP-XXXX to assist in containing spectral anomalies is under consideration."

item.title: Re: NOVEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hey Mikhail Radzinsky, welcome to the SCP wiki! You seem rather soft spoken, but we are glad to have you here and eagerly await your additions to the site! Try not to burn anything while you're here.
As for writing, just make sure you go through the proper greenlighting process on the idea forums first. Remember that there is no rush, and you should take time familiarizing yourself with how Series 6 articles are formatted. We are a rather unique bunch so I'm sure just reading and being a part of the community will be rather fun for you! For my recommendation, you should check out SCP-5005 its one that adds a sense of mystery, and makes you wonder how someone thought this up.

+ Resources
- Hide Resources

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerened, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.

Best of luck!

item.title: Re: greg
item.content:encoded:
Was brought in by request, so here's my take on it.

The SCP itself seems rather disjointed to me I guess? It has these interesting abilities, only to uncontrollably teleport? Why does this happen, is there any reason to it or is it just used as a device to put it into humorous locations? Other than these initial details I don't really have much idea about the entity. Was it created in a lab, or always like this? How does it communicate to researchers and why? A few more details are needed to iron out just exactly what this SCP is.

The narrative part also has me a bit concerned, as there isn't much one. You have a initial containment, underestimating its abilities, then recontainent which I feel I've read several times before. This isn't exactly a bad thing however, you need to put your own unique spin on it. Then the whole makes friends with the doctor, only to have the doctor touch it seems a bit out of character for the Foundation. Usually something that emits a gas that elicits terror in humans would not be allowed to come into touch contact with a researcher. I'll echo a little of what cybersqyd said and ask where is the story leading? Is it building up to something after the doctor is killed, or does the article just end there?

All in all, the idea has potential but could use more refinement as listed above. Hope this helps, best of luck.

item.title: (Seking Greenlight) World of the Wars
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: In various small enclaves around the world, the belligerents of all the world's wars have small military contingents that never surrendered. In truth, these enclaves are actually entrances to an alternate universe that serves solely to keep wars going, and created these enclaves for that purpose. Here, not only do no real-world wars ever end, the various factions have their own political intrigues including new wars, espionage, and support for others.

Central Narrative: Begins with the Foundation's arrival in the holdout of the Obskurakorps, which they think is a more mundane holdout, or at least as mundane as the Obskurakorps can be. Talks end up going hot after the Obskurakorps takes them to be one of their predecessor organisations trying to infiltrate them, resulting in the death of the Obskurakorps' and Wehrmacht's Fuhrer and a war between them as to who will be his successor, and the unfolding use of this as a proxy war by various factions to try to get the side that would be most beneficial to them.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Seeing how societies change with anachronistic influences and eternal war, as well as how the balance of these wars shift and change in response to major events.

Additional Notes: This was largely inspired by post-WWII Japanese Holdouts, although the process of brainstorming it moved it far beyond being all that recognisable. I'm also not sure about having the Nazis be the ones who go into the Civil War, since I'm afraid that might be a bit overdone in alternate history scenarios where they win/don't get completely usurped.

item.title: The Ambivalent Monster
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It's a standard fare weird alternate dimension. They send two D classes down there and spooky monster blah blah, until they realize the "monster" is a fairly reasonable sapient entity though distinctly not humanoid.

Elevator Pitch: It's an exploration of the Foundation's inhuman treatment of D-classes. The Eldritch entity that's down there is more concerned for the D-classes' well being than foundation personnel.

Central Narrative: Two D-classes are sent with cameras to document an extradimensional space (The Foundation at this point, knows it's unescapable, they're just curious). While wandering a mostly empty area, they stumble upon a friendly entity that appears concerned for them. The entity, while free to leave, stays to attempt to help the two get out, communicating back and forth and cooperating with the Foundation. Eventually, when the Entity finds a way to send them back with the help of the Foundation, they're rejected because it would be too costly, leaving the story ending at that.

Additional Notes: This would be a very character focused story. Though the story paints the Foundation in a bad light, I want to avoid the common tropes of the foundation being malicious idiots though, they have legitimate albeit incredibly cold reasons for their decision.

item.title: Re: Philosopher's Blender
item.content:encoded:
Firstly, I would like to thank you for your quick response. I was expecting 1-2 days of waiting until someone review this.

I see, so there would be potential in this SCP idea, potential I was missing. That is…good to know. However, I wasn't just thinking about food, that was mostly just to show how normal people, in this case kitchen staff, would use it. In the long-term, I was thinking about Foundation personnel, for example, mixing together two different blood types to create a totally new blood type, with it's own pros and cons, pros being immunity to most blood-transmited diseases and cons being that the consumer is constantly thirstly unless drinking blood, human or otherwise.

However, stuff like electronics and incompatible things, that's something I was not really thinking about. Thank you for bringing this possibility to my attention. I will dwell on this idea.

As for the narrative side…truthfully, I don't really have an idea how this part should work. Yes, i did look up this forum for other ideas posted by others, however thinking that they might be new members and authors like me, I did not take their example for this part.

How should the central narrative look like? What specific…information should be in it? Like…

The blender is in actuality the experiment of a researcher with a Sc.D in science, who tried to make himself famous. In the end, using the help and resources of a mysterious contributor, he managed to create this blender which, well, mixes together ingredients/materials at an level not yet achieved in modern science. However, said researcher got absorbed, body and mind, into the blender, which now uses his knowledge of science and twisted mind to fine-tune the blending process and create all kinds of unique items. Limited conversation with the researcher can be made using the touchscreen.

That was at least the background for this SCP article. Is that a better example of an central narrative? If so, it's slightly hard to explain in this forum with the 400 words limit…

Nonetheless, I once again thank you for your review.

item.title: Re: Philosopher's Blender
item.content:encoded:
"Magic tool/appliance" and "weird thing that makes more weird things" are both heavily trodden territory on the site, but the concept here might still be viable.

I think you're missing the real potential here, though: A blender that makes super-healthy food isn't really interesting. A blender that blends any two things to produce a new thing resembling both, on the other hand, is very interesting- Blend small electronics. Blend abstract concepts. Blend things with incompatible properties.(say, a lit match and an ice cube) I'd suggest ditching the "decreasing returns" aspect- it doesn't add anything but another reason for the Foundation to put it in a box and ignore it.

On the narrative front- and I apologize for being a bit blunt here in the interest of clarity- what you have right now isn't really a narrative so much as a discovery log, and even within that "it just appeared out of nowhere and then was found by an agent by happenstance" is a site cliche you'll want to avoid. (Compare "It was a dark and stormy night…") It's up to you to figure out what sort of story you can tell using with this thing, but on the upside there's a ton of options. I'd suggest brainstorming in the direction of "mad logic"- What intersection of necessity and drunken wishing might spawn this thing? What would drive a mad scientist to usurp the laws of physics to construct it? What might someone with more curiosity than sense do with it? The answer only needs to make sense to the character; walking us through their chain of decisions in a clever way can be a great basis for a story.
